author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Diagnose corrupted PS2 skyboxes across camera angles and cold boots
summary: Separate a bad sky texture from depth ordering, stale graphics cache, upscaling, and driver behavior by recording a panoramic route at native output and changing one disposable layer at a time.
heroAlt: PCSX2 before-fix scene showing a visible graphics corruption across a large background layer

blocks.text: Record how the corruption follows the camera

A skybox may be a distant mesh, a textured dome, a sequence of background sprites, or a framebuffer layer. Rotate the camera through a full sweep and note whether the defect stays fixed to the screen, follows world direction, appears only near geometry, or changes after an area load. A screen-fixed block suggests composition; a world-fixed seam suggests texture or mesh sampling; flicker at intersections suggests depth ordering.
Clear only cache that the emulator explicitly documents as disposable. Memory cards, in-game saves, profiles, firmware, and game images are not graphics cache.

items: An in-game save in an outdoor area with free camera movement.
A native-resolution panorama captured on a clean title profile.
The renderer, GPU driver, texture-preload, and mipmapping values recorded.
A list of disposable graphics-cache locations from the app's own controls or documentation.
A later outdoor area for independent confirmation.

blocks.text: Distinguish texture, depth, and cached state

items: 1. Cold-boot and rotate the camera slowly through the same landmarks while recording direct output.
2. Reset texture replacements, post-processing, and manual offsets; repeat at native internal resolution.
3. Compare supported hardware APIs while keeping driver and all accuracy values fixed.
4. Use a short software-rendered panorama to establish whether the background data itself is correct.
5. If the failure appears only after a crash or resume, restart Android and rebuild only documented disposable graphics cache once.
6. When upscaling alone exposes seams, step down to the last clean multiplier before evaluating a title-specific sampling fix.
7. Check the second outdoor area for the same world direction, depth intersection, or cache behavior.
8. Archive captures with cold/warm status so a one-time cache rebuild is not mistaken for a permanent fix.

blocks.text: Large backgrounds amplify small coordinate and depth errors. Their texture may remain stable while foreground geometry changes, which makes camera-relative evidence especially useful. Cache rebuilding is justified only when a clean cold run differs from a post-crash run; it should not become a ritual after every visual fault.
A pass requires spatial, lifecycle, and area coverage.

items: The panorama has no new seams, scrambled tiles, or missing sectors.
Foreground geometry occludes the sky in the correct order.
The result survives two cold boots without clearing cache again.
A later outdoor area renders correctly under the same profile.
Internal-resolution changes do not reintroduce unrelated HUD or texture artifacts.
Only post-crash sessions fail: include lifecycle and cache-rebuild evidence.
A single world direction shows a seam above native resolution: report the exact multiplier and camera bearing.
Software output is also corrupt on a verified image: test clean patches and game progression.
The sky changes with a custom driver only: return to system driver and isolate that package.

blocks.text: Return to the system driver, original hardware API, automatic texture controls, and last clean resolution. If cache backup is supported, restore its metadata only when rebuilding made behavior worse; otherwise allow the emulator to regenerate disposable data once from a cold start.
Cloud and weather changes need matched saves
Games may animate weather or choose sky variants from time, mission state, or random seeds. Compare the same in-game save and route so legitimate background changes are not labeled corruption.
